sections.label: Infrastructure & Utilities
sections.summary: Utility infrastructure requires specifications for transformer placement and equipment spacing, underground utility separation distances, property boundary/easement coordination, and construction safety notification procedures.

sections.label: Building Design & Setbacks
sections.summary: Critical clearance requirements for building envelope, driveways, and site structures from overhead electrical conductors must be documented with surveyed elevations and mid-span measurements.

sections.label: Street Trees & Landscaping
sections.summary: Tree species, sizing, and clearance documentation requirements from overhead electrical lines and underground utilities must be clarified with dimensional specifications and voltage classification information.

comments.headline: Building proximity and structural clearance documentation
comments.summary: Transformer pad locations lack documented horizontal and vertical clearances to adjacent buildings, structures, fences, and architectural features. Minimum 5-foot clearance to buildings and special clearance requirements (reduced 3-foot to masonry with AE approval, 12-foot to windows/doors/ducts on oil-filled equipment) are not dimensioned on plans.
comments.crossDep: Architecture must provide building elevations, window/door locations, and equipment access paths to coordinate clearances with electrical design.
comments.attn: Determine whether any pads are proposed with reduced clearances less than 5 feet; if so, Austin Energy Design written approval and 3-hour fire-rating documentation must be obtained before plan approval.

details.text: Transformer pad locations shown but measured clearances to adjacent buildings and structures not documented or dimensioned on plans. Minimum 5-foot clearance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown but clearance dimensions to buildings are not documented. Submit detailed plan sheets showing measured clearances from each transformer pad to all adjacent buildings and structures.
Transformer pad locations shown but pad dimensions and horizontal clearances to buildings not dimensioned on plans. Cannot verify minimum 5-foot clearance requirement.

Transformer pads shown on electrical plan but without any documented clearance measurements or dimension callouts to verify 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from buildings, structures, and foundations. Applicant must provide dimensioned site plan or construction details showing clearances from each pad to adjacent structures.

details.text: Retaining walls are present on site but clearance dimensions from transformer pads to all adjacent retaining walls not provided.

runComments.comment: Retaining walls are present on site. Submit clearance dimensions from transformer pads to all adjacent retaining walls, demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance where applicable.

details.text: Transformer Pad 4 located very close to southern property fence without documented clearances. Access door orientation not identified; cannot determine whether 5-foot (access-door side) or 3-foot (non-access side) clearance applies.

runComments.comment: Fences are shown on site. Submit clearance dimensions from transformer pads to fences, and identify transformer access door orientation to verify compliance with differential clearance requirements (5 feet vs. 3 feet per UCM § 1.10.4).
Clearances from transformer pads to any adjacent fences not dimensioned; transformer operator/control designations not identified.

Transformer Pad 4 is positioned very close to the southern property line wood fence with no documented clearance measurements. Applicant must provide dimensioned clearances from the pad to the adjacent fence, and clarify the access door orientation to determine whether 5-foot clearance (if operators/controls side) or 3-foot clearance (if non-access side) applies. If clearance is less than required, additional setback or fence modification must be documented.

details.text: If any transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to brick or masonry buildings, no Austin Energy Design written approval, 3-hour fire-rating documentation, confined-space verification, or window/door/duct clearance (10-foot minimum lateral, 15-foot vertical) documentation is provided.

runComments.comment: No reduced clearances (less than 5 feet) are documented on the submitted plans. If the applicant intends to use reduced 3-foot clearances to brick/masonry buildings, submit Austin Energy Design written approval and architectural specifications documenting 3-hour fire rating in the clearance area.
No reduced clearances shown; documentation of AE Design approval and required conditions not provided.

If any transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to brick or masonry buildings, the plans must include documentation of: (1) written Austin Energy Design approval, (2) verification of minimum 3-hour fire rating in the clearance area (from architectural specifications), (3) confirmation that the location is not in a confined space, (4) verification of minimum 10 feet clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (5) verification of minimum 15 feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts. No such documentation is currently provided.

details.text: Building elevations and sections not provided. No verification that balconies, overhangs, or covered structures maintain minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from transformer pads or that no structures exist directly above pads.

runComments.comment: No balcony or overhang clearance documentation is provided. If balconies or overhangs exist above or adjacent to transformer pads, submit building elevations or cross-sections demonstrating minimum 5-foot lateral clearance and confirming no structures directly above pads.
Building elevations and sections not provided; no clearances shown from balconies or overhangs to transformer pads.

If balconies or overhangs exist on adjacent buildings within 5 feet of any transformer pads, provide building elevation views confirming minimum 5-foot lateral clearance and verification that no coverings or structures exist directly above pad or minimum equipment area.

details.text: Building elevations not submitted; transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) not specified. Cannot verify 12-foot minimum horizontal clearance from oil-filled equipment to windows, doors, and ventilating ducts on adjacent buildings.

runComments.comment: No building elevations or transformer type specifications are provided. Submit building elevation sheets showing window, door, and ventilation locations, transformer equipment specifications identifying whether oil-filled, and measured clearance distances demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 (12 feet minimum for oil-filled equipment when clearance conditions are met).
Building elevations not provided; window/door locations unknown; transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs dry-type) not specified.

Applicant must provide building elevations and electrical equipment specifications (oil-filled vs. dry-type) for each transformer. If windows, doors, or ventilating ducts exist on adjacent buildings, provide dimensioned clearances showing minimum 12-foot horizontal clearance from edge of oil-filled equipment pad when window/door/duct is less than 12 feet from grade or has less than 5 feet lateral separation.

comments.headline: Construction safety clearances and utility notification requirement
comments.summary: Site logistics or construction phasing plan must document staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, and work platforms with verified 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law. Cover sheet or general notes must include statement requiring owner/contractor to notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before construction near high-voltage overhead lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
comments.crossDep: Contractor and site safety manager responsible for maintaining clearances and providing utility notification
comments.attn: Verify construction phasing plan accounts for overhead line constraints; confirm Austin Energy contact information for cover sheet note

details.text: Site logistics plan or construction phasing plan must show construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platform locations with verified 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements.

runComments.comment: A site logistics plan or construction phasing plan must be submitted showing staging areas, equipment laydown zones, crane swing radius, material storage, and scaffold locations, with explicit notation that all construction activities maintain minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2.

Construction logistics plan or site phasing plan must document staging area boundaries, crane swing radius zones, equipment laydown areas, and work platforms with dimension annotations verifying 10-foot radial clearance from all overhead electric lines. Construction management notes must address overhead line safety during all phases.

Site logistics or construction phasing plan must show construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platform locations with verified 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines per OSHA and Texas law requirements.

details.text: Cover sheet or general notes must include statement: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.

runComments.comment: A plan note must be added to the cover sheet or general notes stating: 'The owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.

Add note to cover sheet or general notes: 'Owner/contractor shall notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any construction activities or operations near overhead electric lines. Contact Austin Energy at [number] per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'

Plans must include a note stating: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.

comments.headline: Underground and gas utility separation distances
comments.summary: Underground utility routing and separation distances from transformer pads are not documented. Minimum 12-inch (OD-to-OD) clearance to non-gas utilities and 24-36 inch clearance to gas pipelines (per pressure) are not verified. Vertical crossing relationships and utility conflict analysis not provided.
comments.crossDep: All underground utility providers (gas, telecom, cable, reclaimed water, etc.) must coordinate clearances. Austin Energy Design may require utility separation study or cross-section coordination.
comments.attn: Confirm whether gas service is provided to site. Prepare comprehensive underground utility separation table and cross-section drawings per UCM § 1.10.5.A and 1.10.5.B.

details.text: If gas service is provided, gas line locations on utility plans not verified. Minimum 24-inch clearance (gas ≤60 psi) or 36-inch clearance (>60 psi high-pressure) from transformer pads not documented.

runComments.comment: If gas service is provided, confirm the presence of gas lines on utility plans and provide minimum horizontal clearance dimensions (24 inches for gas pipelines less than 60 psi, 36 inches for high-pressure gas 60 psi and over) from transformer pads.

details.text: Underground utility routing (telecom, cable, reclaimed water, and other utilities) shown on utility plans (Sheet 19) but horizontal and vertical separation from transformer pads (minimum 12-inch OD-to-OD clearance) not dimensioned.

runComments.comment: Underground utility routing is shown on utility plans but clearance dimensions from transformer pads are not provided. Submit clearance dimensions demonstrating minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical separation from transformer pads to other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam) per UCM § 1.10.5.A.
Underground utility routing shown but horizontal and vertical clearances from transformer pads not dimensioned.

Provide comprehensive utility coordination table or drawing showing horizontal and vertical separation from each transformer pad to all underground utilities including telecom, cable, reclaimed water (if present), and any other utilities not specifically covered under the 5-foot water/wastewater/storm drain requirements. Minimum 12-inch clearance (OD to OD) must be documented.

details.text: Utility coordination analysis missing: no documentation that transformer pads and AE underground facilities do not cross over/under other utilities, or that buildings and foundations are not constructed over AE facilities.

runComments.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical relationships between transformer pads, AE facilities, and other utilities are not provided. Submit utility cross-sections demonstrating that transformer pads and AE underground facilities do not cross over/under other utility lines, and that buildings/foundations are not constructed over AE facilities, per UCM § 1.10.5.B.
Cross-section/profile drawings not provided; utility crossing relationships not documented.

Provide utility coordination analysis confirming: (1) transformer pads and AE underground facilities do not cross under/over other utility lines, (2) no customer buildings, foundations, or structures (including footings) are located over or immediately adjacent to AE underground electrical facilities, and (3) adequate vertical separation is maintained between all utilities.

comments.headline: Vault transformer niche installation specifications
comments.summary: If the labeled 'Vault Easement' transformer (near Building 8) is a niche service installation, required documentation for fire-wall rating, ventilation specifications, and Austin Energy Design approval are not provided.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design must confirm vault configuration (pad-mounted vs. niche). Architecture must provide fire-wall and ventilation specifications.
comments.attn: CRITICAL: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether the 'Vault Easement' transformer near Bldg 8 is a niche installation. If yes, this becomes a blocking issue requiring fire-rating and ventilation documentation. If no, these findings may not be applicable.

details.text: If vault transformer is niche configuration, no cross-section drawings showing minimum 35-foot vertical clearance inside niche entrance provided.

runComments.comment: One transformer is labeled as a vault configuration ('Vault Easement'). If this is a niche service installation, submit cross-section drawings demonstrating minimum 35-foot vertical clearance inside niche and niche entrance per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 3.

details.text: If vault transformer is niche configuration, no architectural specifications documenting 3-hour fire-wall ratings, ventilation specifications, or evidence of Austin Energy Design business unit consultation provided.

runComments.comment: If the vault transformer is a niche service installation, submit: (1) architectural specifications documenting 3-hour fire wall ratings, (2) ventilation specifications, and (3) evidence of consultation with Austin Energy Design business unit per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 3.

All dimension lines must originate at the outside conductor, not pole center.
comments.crossDep: Coordinate with registered surveyor and utility for conductor elevation data
comments.attn: Verify surveyor will conduct site survey to obtain existing pole locations and mid-span conductor elevations

details.text: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and labeled clearance dimensions must be provided showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductors to all building faces.

runComments.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and labeled clearance dimensions are required to verify the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement per UCM § 1.10.3.

Surveyed elevations of existing overhead conductors and building elevation drawings showing clearance dimensions are required to verify 7'6" sky-to-ground clearance is maintained from conductors to building faces and projections.

Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions must be provided to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained from all buildings to existing overhead electric conductors.

runComments.comment: Building elevation sheets showing all building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) with dimensions and clearance verification from overhead electric conductors are required.

Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations showing clearances from conductors to all building projections (roofs, parapets, overhangs, decks, patios) must be provided.

Building elevation drawings must show all building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, patios) with clearance dimensions to overhead electric conductors demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained.

runComments.comment: Building elevations with labeled clearance dimensions from overhead electric facilities in adjacent ROW must be provided, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
Austin Energy utility plan showing exact location of overhead facilities in adjacent ROW with clearance dimensions from buildings must be provided.

Building elevation sheets must show surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimensions demonstrating buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from electric facilities in adjacent right-of-way.

details.text: Building elevation sheets prepared by registered surveyor must include surveyed elevations and locations of existing overhead conductors with dimension annotations showing clearances. Sheets must be sealed by both registered surveyor and engineer.

runComments.comment: Building elevation sheets must be submitted, including registered surveyor data showing surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.

Building elevation sheets prepared by registered surveyor must include surveyed elevations and locations of existing overhead conductors with dimension annotations showing clearances to building components.

Building elevation sheets showing surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations must be provided to demonstrate required clearances are met. These sheets must be sealed by a registered surveyor and engineer.

details.text: Section and plan view exhibits must show dimension lines originating at the outside conductor location and extending to the outermost edge of each building and building projection, with dimension lines extending from the conductor, not pole center.

runComments.comment: Section and plan view exhibits must be added showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of each building and building projection for clearance verification per UCM § 1.10.3. Dimension lines must originate at the outside conductor location, not pole center.

Provide enlarged plan details and section views with dimension lines extending from outside conductor to outermost edges of all buildings and building projections, demonstrating required clearance envelopes are maintained.

Section and plan view exhibits with dimension lines from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections must be provided for all proposed structures within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.

details.text: All clearance dimension annotations must explicitly show that dimensions are measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline. Dimension lines must originate clearly at the outer conductor location.

runComments.comment: All clearance dimension lines must originate at the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from pole center or centerline of multi-conductor installations. On three-phase installations, the conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension line endpoints must clearly show measurement origin at the conductor location.

All clearance dimension annotations must explicitly originate at the outside conductor location, not at the utility pole centerline or pole face. Dimension lines and callouts must clearly show measurement origin point (e.g., '15'-0" from outside conductor').

Any clearance dimension annotations must explicitly show that dimensions are measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline. Dimension lines must originate at the outer conductor location.

comments.headline: Driveway vertical clearances and surveyor mid-span measurements required
comments.summary: Registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements must be provided showing vertical distance from lowest point of overhead facilities (including conductors, attachments, and telecommunications cables) to finished driveway grades and parking areas, with section views demonstrating 16-foot (parking only) or 18-foot (truck traffic) clearance.
comments.crossDep: Coordinate with surveyor on pole and conductor elevation data; verify anticipated vehicle types (trucks vs. passenger vehicles only)
comments.attn: Clarify whether parking areas will accommodate trucks; if yes, 18-foot clearance required per UCM § 1.10.6.2

details.text: Vertical clearance dimensions must be provided for the driveway where the OHE line crosses, showing minimum 16-foot clearance (no truck traffic) or 18-foot (with truck traffic) from lowest point of overhead electric line including all attachments to finished driveway grade.

runComments.comment: Vertical clearance dimensions must be provided for the driveway where the OHE line crosses, showing minimum 16-foot or 18-foot clearance from the lowest point of the overhead electric line (including any attachments) to the finished driveway grade. Registered surveyor data for mid-span clearance verification is required.

Registered surveyor mid-span clearance data must be provided showing vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead facilities (including all conductors and attachments) to finished driveway grades. Section views must show 16-foot clearance for parking without truck traffic or 18-foot for areas with truck traffic.

Grading plan and section views must show vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including telecommunications attachments) to finished driveway grade, demonstrating 16-foot minimum (18-foot if truck traffic).

details.text: If parking or vehicle display areas are positioned beneath overhead electric lines, section views with labeled vertical clearance dimensions must be provided showing the required clearance (16 feet for residential/pedestrian parking, 18 feet if truck traffic anticipated).

runComments.comment: If parking or vehicle display areas are positioned beneath overhead electric lines, section views with labeled vertical clearance dimensions must be provided to demonstrate the required clearance (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic).

details.text: Registered surveyor clearance survey showing pole locations and mid-span clearances from overhead facilities to driveways, parking areas, and buildings must be provided to verify all vertical clearance requirements (7.5-foot, 16-foot, 18-foot) are satisfied.

runComments.comment: Registered surveyor data must be provided showing pole locations, overhead conductor elevations, and mid-span clearance measurements for the driveway crossing. This data is essential to verify the minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance requirement per UCM § 1.10.6.2.

Registered surveyor must provide documented mid-span clearance measurements for existing overhead facilities showing vertical distance from lowest point of conductors and attachments to highest proposed site features (building roofs, HVAC equipment, etc.) to demonstrate code-required clearances are maintained.

Registered surveyor clearance survey showing pole locations and mid-span clearances from overhead facilities to driveways, parking areas, and buildings must be provided to verify all vertical clearance requirements (7.5-foot, 16-foot, 18-foot) are satisfied.

comments.headline: Tree species and landscape feature clearances from overhead lines
comments.summary: All trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors must be verified as utility-compatible species per ECM Appendix F (marked 'UC', generally ≤20 feet mature height). Currently proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are not utility-compatible. Trees must be relocated beyond 10 feet or replaced with utility-compatible species. Decorative lighting fixtures require clearance verification if positioned beneath overhead lines.
comments.crossDep: Coordinate with landscape architect on tree relocation or species substitution
comments.attn: Confirm whether proposed tree species have been reviewed for utility compatibility; ECM Appendix F required for verification

details.text: All trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors must be from Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC'). Currently proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are not utility-compatible. Trees must be relocated beyond 10 feet of conductors or replaced with utility-compatible species per ECM § 2.4.1.D and UCM § 1.10.10.4.

runComments.comment: All trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors must be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC'). The currently proposed species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) are not utility-compatible. Trees must either be relocated to positions more than 10 feet from conductors, or replaced with utility-compatible species verified in ECM Appendix F 'UC' column.

Plant schedule must specify which tree species are utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F for planting within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors. Tree species must be marked or noted as 'UC' (Utility Compatible, generally ≤20' mature height). Plan must include dimension annotations showing lateral distance (horizontal) from each tree location to the overhead conductor and note species compliance with utility compatibility requirement.

Landscape plan must verify that all trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors (per more restrictive UCM 50-foot standard) are species marked 'UC' (Utility Compatible) in ECM Appendix F, generally mature height ≤20 feet. Annotate lateral distances.

runComments.comment: Photometric plan or enlarged lighting detail must show locations of all decorative light fixtures near overhead electric lines with dimension annotations verifying clearance requirements are met (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 15-foot radial), or notes indicating fixtures are relocated away from lines.

Photometric plan or site plan must show decorative lighting fixture locations with clearance verification demonstrating 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from overhead lines, or relocation notes if conflicts exist.

comments.crossDep: Water Utility, Wastewater Utility, and Stormwater Departments must verify no conflicts between transformer locations and service lines. May require utility coordination drawings or formal separation approval.
comments.attn: Prepare utility coordination table or cross-reference drawing comparing electrical plan (Sheet 21) with water/wastewater (Sheet 19) and stormwater (Sheet 12) plans.

details.text: Water service lines shown on utility plan (Sheet 19) but horizontal clearances from transformer pads (minimum 5-foot) not dimensioned on electrical plan (Sheet 21).

runComments.comment: Water lines are shown on utility plan. Submit clearance dimensions demonstrating minimum 5-foot horizontal separation from transformer pads to water lines per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2.
Water line routing shown but horizontal clearances from transformer pads not dimensioned.

Provide utility coordination drawing or table showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to water service lines. Dimensions on electrical plan must verify clearances from all pad edges to nearest water utility.

details.text: Wastewater line routing shown but horizontal clearances from transformer pads and cleanouts (minimum 5-foot) not dimensioned on electrical plan.

runComments.comment: Wastewater lines are shown on utility plan. Submit clearance dimensions demonstrating minimum 5-foot horizontal separation from transformer pads to wastewater lines per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2.
Wastewater line routing shown but horizontal clearances from transformer pads not dimensioned.

Provide utility coordination drawing or table showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to wastewater service lines and cleanouts. Dimensions on electrical plan must verify clearances from all pad edges to nearest wastewater utility.

details.text: Storm drain infrastructure shown on utility plans (Sheets 12 and 19) but horizontal clearances from transformer pads (minimum 5-foot) not dimensioned on electrical plan (Sheet 21).

runComments.comment: Storm drain infrastructure is shown on utility plans. Submit clearance dimensions demonstrating minimum 5-foot horizontal separation from transformer pads to storm drain lines per UCM § 2.9.1.B.2.
Storm drain routing shown but horizontal clearances from transformer pads not dimensioned.

Provide utility coordination showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to storm drain lines. Cross-reference electrical plan with storm sewer plan (Sheet 12) with dimensions verifying all clearances.

comments.headline: Property boundaries, easements, and electrical routing location verification
comments.summary: Transformer pad locations relative to property boundaries, recorded easements, and electrical routing are not explicitly documented. Confirmation that all pads and routing are 100% on private property and outside recorded easements is not provided. Transformer easement boundaries not depicted for most pad locations.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design must confirm transformer easement width and accessibility requirements. Title company or surveyor may need to verify recorded easement boundaries.
comments.attn: Cross-reference property plat (Sheet 2) and site plans (Sheets 9, 21) to verify all pad and routing locations. Obtain recorded easement instrument numbers and prepare compliance documentation.

details.text: Transformer pads shown on electrical plan but distance from property boundaries not dimensioned. Confirmation that all pads are 100% on private property and do not straddle property lines not documented.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad property location is not explicitly documented. Submit plan sheets with dimension callouts confirming all transformer pads are located 100% on private property and do not straddle property lines per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4.
Property line relationships to transformer pads not dimensioned; confirmation that all pads are 100% on private property not documented.

Provide explicit notation or dimension table on electrical plan confirming: (1) each transformer pad is located 100% on private property (with distance from property boundary), (2) no pad is located in public right-of-way, and (3) no pad straddles a property line. Cross-reference property boundaries from plat (Sheet 2) with pad locations on electrical plan (Sheet 21).

details.text: Transformer pad positions relative to recorded drainage, water, sewer, and overhead electric easements not verified. If any pad is located within a prohibited easement, Austin Energy Design written approval not provided.
details.citation: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 (property requirement); easement-specific regulations

runComments.comment: Transformer pad locations relative to easements are not explicitly documented. Submit plan sheets with notes identifying whether any transformer pads are located in drainage, water, sewer, or electrical easements, and provide Austin Energy Design written approval if required per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4.
Easement locations documented on plat but transformer pad positions relative to easements not verified; no confirmation of clearance from prohibited easement areas.

Provide easement compliance analysis confirming: (1) each transformer pad location relative to recorded easements (drainage, water, sewer, overhead electric), (2) if any pad is located within a prohibited easement, provide written Austin Energy Design approval, or (3) revise plans to locate all pads outside easement boundaries. Reference recorded easement instrument numbers and provide cross-referenced site plan showing easement boundaries overlaid with transformer pad locations.

details.text: Transformer easement boundaries not depicted on site plan for most pads (only one 'Vault Easement' labeled). Required easement width and accessibility requirements not coordinated with Austin Energy Design.

runComments.comment: Transformer easements are not documented for most pads (only one 'Vault Easement' is labeled). Submit plat or easement exhibit showing transformer easement boundaries around all four pads with dimensions sufficient for Austin Energy accessibility per UCM § 1.10.3.
Transformer easements not shown for 4 of 5 pads; easement widths and accessibility requirements not documented.

Applicant must: (1) coordinate with Austin Energy Design to determine the required transformer easement width for each pad, (2) depict transformer easement boundaries (not just note 'additional easements may be required') on the site plan and electrical plan, (3) document easement width in plan notes, and (4) ensure easement boundaries are not in conflict with recorded property easements or other site features.

details.text: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters not verified as 100% on private property. Routing shown but no notation or dimension callouts confirming no portion in public right-of-way.

runComments.comment: Electrical routing property boundaries are not documented. Submit plan sheets with notes and dimension callouts confirming all electrical routing from transformers to meters is 100% on private property per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4.
Electrical service routing from transformer to meter not verified as 100% on private property; no routing callouts or property line clearance dimensions provided.

Provide notation on electrical plan confirming that 100% of electrical routing from each transformer pad to its associated meter(s) is located on private property, with no portion in public right-of-way. Include cross-reference to property boundaries from site plan (Sheet 9) and plat (Sheet 2).

comments.headline: Transformer access door orientation and installation requirements
comments.summary: Access door orientation and confined-space installation requirements are not documented on plans. Hot-stick operation clearance (minimum 10 feet) and niche installation specifications (vertical clearance, fire rating, ventilation) are not addressed.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design must approve transformer access configuration and clearances. Architecture must confirm niche fire-wall ratings and ventilation specifications.
comments.attn: Identify which pads (if any) are located in niche configurations. Confirm with AE Design whether all pads are pad-mounted (not niche) or if any require niche-specific documentation.

details.text: Transformer access door orientation not identified on electrical plan. Dimensioned clearances from access-door sides to open areas or adjacent buildings (minimum 10-foot for hot-stick use area) not documented for all pads.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown but access door orientation is not identified. Submit detailed site plan sheets showing transformer access door orientation and dimensions demonstrating minimum 10-foot clearance from hot-stick use area (access door side) to open area or adjacent building per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4.
Access door orientations not identified; hot-stick clearance dimensions not shown.

Applicant must clearly identify the access door orientation (with directional arrow or note) for each transformer pad on the electrical plan, and provide dimensioned measurements from the access door side of each pad to the nearest open area or adjacent building/structure, confirming minimum 10-foot clearance in the hot-stick use area.

details.text: If any transformer is located in confined space/niche configuration (enclosed on 3+ sides), no cross-section drawings demonstrating 35-foot vertical clearance inside niche entrance or 3-hour fire-wall and ventilation specifications provided.

runComments.comment: No niche or enclosed area transformer configurations are indicated on submitted plans. If any transformer is located in a confined space (enclosed on 3+ sides), submit cross-section drawings demonstrating 15-foot vertical clearance per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4.
Niche/enclosed area configuration not documented; building cross-sections not provided.

If any transformer locations involve niches (equipment accessible from outside but within building footprint) or enclosed/notched-out building configurations, provide cross-section drawings demonstrating minimum 35-foot vertical clearance from grade through entire access path, and provide documentation of 3-hour fire wall rating and ventilation specifications.

comments.headline: Transformer pad specifications, grading, and vehicle protection
comments.summary: Transformer pad dimensions, equipment specifications, drainage details, and bollard protection for parking-adjacent locations are not documented. Austin Energy Design-approved pad details and equipment type specifications are not provided. Surface drainage for oil-filled transformers not documented.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design must provide transformer pad details and approve service specifications. Site design must confirm parking proximity and bollard placement.
comments.attn: Obtain transformer pad details from Austin Energy Design business unit. Confirm whether any pads are within 4 feet of parking areas; if so, bollard specifications must match AE Design equipment pad standards.

details.text: Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) not specified on electrical plan. For oil-filled equipment, grading plan with drainage arrows and minimum 1% slope away from buildings and adjacent structures not documented.

runComments.comment: Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. If oil-filled transformers are proposed, submit grading plan notes and arrow callouts demonstrating that surface drainage flows away from transformer pads and building structures per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1.
Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs dry-type) not specified; transformer locations not shown on grading plan; surface drainage direction not documented at transformer locations.

Applicant must: (1) specify on electrical plan whether each transformer is oil-filled or dry-type, (2) for oil-filled equipment, provide grading plan with drainage arrows and slope percentages at each pad location confirming liquid flow is directed away from buildings and adjacent structures, and (3) confirm minimum 1% slope away from all pad locations.

details.text: Transformer pad detail sheets matching Austin Energy Design specifications not provided. Pad dimensions, service type (single-phase vs. three-phase), equipment specifications, and AE Design approval documents not submitted.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad detail sheets matching Austin Energy Design specifications are not provided. Submit AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets for each pad showing: (1) service type (single-phase or three-phase), (2) pad dimensions (width x depth), (3) equipment specifications, and (4) any special installation requirements per UCM § 1.5.2.6.
Transformer pad dimensions not shown; service type (single-phase vs three-phase) not specified; AE Design pad detail sheets not provided.

Applicant must: (1) obtain Austin Energy Design approval documents and transformer pad detail sheets for each of the 4 transformer pads, (2) confirm the service type (single-phase or three-phase) for each pad and the associated electrical load, (3) depict the AE Design-approved pad dimensions (length × width) on the electrical plan for each pad, and (4) provide the approved detail sheets as part of the plan set (reference from electrical plan detail callouts).

details.text: For all transformer pads within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle circulation, no dimension callouts or bollard detail sheets provided. Bollard specifications (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts with equipment-door-opening spacing) not documented.

runComments.comment: Bollard specifications and clearance determinations are not provided. For all transformer pads within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle circulation routes, submit: (1) dimension callouts confirming distances to parking/circulation areas, and (2) bollard detail sheets showing 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts with spacing that allows equipment access door opening per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4.
Clearances from transformer pads to parking areas not dimensioned; bollard details and specifications not shown.

Applicant must: (1) provide dimensioned measurements on electrical plan showing distance from each transformer pad to nearest parking stall or vehicle circulation route, (2) for any pad within 4 feet of parking/circulation areas, provide bollard details referencing AE Design equipment pad specifications showing: 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts, spacing that allows equipment door opening, and installation details, or (3) if no bollards are required, document that all pads are more than 4 feet from parking/vehicle areas.

comments.headline: Electrical equipment clearances and working space deficiencies
comments.summary: Electrical meter locations and transformer equipment require detailed documentation of working clearances and clearance from overhead conductors. Meter locations must maintain 30-inch-wide clear access space, 36-inch front depth, and 6.5-foot headroom with no obstructions. Transformers must maintain 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors.
comments.crossDep: Coordinate with electrical engineer and utility on meter location requirements and transformer specifications
comments.attn: Verify utility meter access requirements; confirm whether pad-mounted or pole-mounted transformers are proposed

details.text: Enlarged meter detail views must show 30-inch front width, 36-inch front depth, and 6.5-foot headroom clearances around each meter location, confirming no site features, fences, walls, vegetation, or building projections obstruct access per UCM § 1.9.3.1.

runComments.comment: Enlarged detail drawings of proposed meter locations must be provided showing no obstructions to meter access and working clearances: minimum 30 inches wide, 36 inches deep front access space, and 6.5 feet headroom per UCM § 1.10.9.

Enlarged meter detail views must show 30-inch front width, 36-inch front depth, and 6.5-foot headroom clearances around each meter location, confirming no site features, fences, walls, vegetation, or building projections obstruct access.

Electrical plan details must verify that meter access areas maintain required working clearances: 30-inch-wide clear space, 36-inch front depth, 6.5-foot headroom, with no obstructions from fences, walls, equipment, vegetation, or building projections.

details.text: Electrical plan section views must show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead line conductors to the top of all proposed transformer equipment, demonstrating 7.5-foot minimum sky-to-ground clearance.

runComments.comment: Electrical design plan must specify transformer types (pole-mounted or pad-mounted) and provide section views with dimension annotations showing vertical clearance from overhead line conductors to top of transformer equipment, verifying 7.5-foot minimum clearance.
Electrical plan section views must show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead line conductors to the top of all transformer equipment, demonstrating 7.5-foot minimum sky-to-ground clearance.

comments.headline: Down guy wire anchor conflicts and easement documentation
comments.summary: Down guy wire anchor locations from existing utility poles must be clearly identified on site plan. Anchors must not conflict with proposed accessible paths and driveways; if conflicts exist, poles must be relocated or converted to self-supporting structures. Dedicated easements (10-foot-wide, extending minimum 5 feet past where guy wire enters ground) must be shown on easement exhibit.
comments.crossDep: Coordinate with utility company on pole relocation or self-supporting conversion if guy wire conflicts arise
comments.attn: Verify whether utility pole modifications (relocation or conversion) require utility coordination; confirm down guy anchor locations from site survey

details.text: Site plan must show down guy wire anchor locations from existing distribution poles and verify they do not conflict with proposed accessible paths or driveways. If conflicts exist, plans must show pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles.

runComments.comment: Down guy wire locations and anchors must be clearly identified on the site plan relative to all proposed accessible paths and driveways. Any conflicts must be resolved through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles, with details and relocation notes provided.

Site plan must clearly identify existing down guy wire anchor locations and document resolution of any conflicts with proposed accessible routes and driveways through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting poles, or provide plan notes confirming no conflicts exist.

Site plan must show down guy wire anchor locations from existing poles and verify they do not conflict with proposed accessible paths or driveways. If conflicts exist, plans must show pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles.

details.text: Easement exhibit and plat must identify and show 10-foot-wide dedicated down guy anchor easements extending minimum 5 feet past where each guy wire support cable enters the ground, per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards.

runComments.comment: Dedicated easements for down guy anchors must be clearly shown on the easement exhibit, displaying 10-foot width and minimum 5-foot extension past where the guy wire enters the ground, per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards.
Easement exhibit and plat must identify and show 10-foot-wide down guy anchor easements extending minimum 5 feet past ground entry point for each down guy support cable on property.
Easement exhibit must show dedicated easements for any down guy anchors from existing distribution poles, 10 feet wide extending minimum 5 feet past where anchor enters ground.

comments.headline: Utility infrastructure coordination and clearance documentation
comments.summary: Water line routing, water meter locations, building foundations, utility pole positions, and elevated walkways must maintain documented clearances from overhead electric facilities. Site plan must show utility pole locations with clearance dimensions to driveways (30-foot separation preferred). Water lines and meters require clearance verification from overhead service drops. Electric easement boundaries must be shown with confirmation that no structures/features are proposed over easement; items within easement must maintain 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor.
comments.crossDep: Water utility must provide location data for existing service lines and meters; ROW/right-of-way management for easement coordination
comments.attn: Verify whether water service drops exist beneath or near driveway; confirm electric easement boundaries with utility

details.text: Site plan must clearly show the location of all existing utility poles and provide dimension annotations indicating clearance from driveway edges. If any poles are within 30 feet of driveway edge, relocation plans must be noted.

runComments.comment: Site plan must clearly show the location of all existing utility poles and provide dimension annotations indicating clearance from driveway edges. If any poles are within 30 feet of driveway edge, relocation plans must be noted.

Plans must clearly indicate whether existing electric poles conflict with proposed driveway alignments. If conflicts exist, relocation notes or revised pole locations must be shown with minimum 30-foot separation from driveway edge.

details.text: Plans must include Austin Energy electric easement exhibit showing easement boundaries with notes confirming no buildings or permanent structures are proposed under or over overhead distribution facilities. Items within easement boundaries must maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor.

runComments.comment: Plans must include Austin Energy easement exhibit showing electric easement boundaries with notes confirming no buildings or permanent structures are proposed under or over overhead distribution facilities, and that items within easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor.

details.text: Utility plan must show locations of overhead electric service-drop lines with dimension annotations verifying 7.5-foot clearance from service drop conductors to water meter locations.

runComments.comment: Utility plan must show locations of overhead electric service-drop lines with dimension annotations verifying 7.5-foot clearance from service drop conductors to water meter locations.
Utility plan must show clearance dimensions from water meter locations to existing overhead electric service drop conductors, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.

details.text: Utility plan must show clearance dimensions between proposed water line routing and existing overhead distribution poles and conductors, documenting adequate separation.

runComments.comment: Clearance dimensions must be provided showing water line routing maintains adequate separation from overhead distribution poles and conductors.
Utility plan must include dimension annotations showing clearance distances from water line routing to all overhead electric poles and conductors.
Utility plan must show clearance dimensions between proposed water line routing and existing overhead distribution poles and conductors.

details.text: Plans must verify that permanent structure foundations within 5 feet of property line allow adequate clearance space (typically 5-7 feet from property line) for installation and maintenance of electric facilities in adjacent ROW or easement areas.

runComments.comment: If any building foundations are located within 5 feet of the property line, detailed dimensions showing clearance space for electric facility access and maintenance must be provided.

Plans must verify that permanent structure foundations within 5 feet of property line allow adequate clearance space (typically 5-7 feet from property line) for installation and maintenance of electric facilities in adjacent ROW or easement areas.

details.text: Site plan must clearly document clearances from proposed buildings and structures to existing streetlight pole locations, verifying poles do not conflict with proposed construction.

runComments.comment: If existing streetlight poles are located near proposed buildings, clearance dimensions must be provided showing building location and pole proximity.
Site plan must clearly document clearances from proposed buildings and structures to existing streetlight pole locations.

details.text: Section views and plan dimensions must demonstrate that elevated walkways and platforms maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the outside conductor of overhead distribution facilities.

runComments.comment: If any elevated walkways, stairs, or platforms are proposed, provide section views with dimension annotations showing 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor.
Section views and plan dimensions must demonstrate that elevated walkways and platforms maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the outside conductor of overhead distribution facilities.

comments.headline: Fence and perimeter element clearances from overhead lines
comments.summary: Fence face alignment and fence post locations must maintain minimum clearances from overhead electric conductors and utility poles: 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from conductor to fence face, and 10-foot clearance from fence posts to pole centerlines. Dimension annotations must be provided on site plan.
comments.attn: Verify whether fences along southern property boundary (near ROW) will obstruct existing pole maintenance access

details.text: Plan must include dimension annotations showing 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from outside conductor to fence face, measured from conductor location not from pole centerline.

runComments.comment: Plan must include dimension annotations showing 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from outside conductor to fence face, measured from conductor location not from pole centerline.
Plan dimensions must show fence alignments maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor (not from pole centerline) of existing overhead electric facilities.

details.text: Dimension annotations must show fence post locations maintain minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from existing electric utility pole centers. Pole locations must be clearly identified on site plan.

runComments.comment: Dimension annotations must be provided showing fence post locations maintain minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from existing electric poles.
Site plan must clearly identify existing utility pole locations and provide dimension annotations showing minimum 10-foot clearance from fence posts to pole centerlines.
Plan view dimensions must demonstrate fence post locations maintain minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from existing electric utility pole centers.

details.text: Enlarged plan details must show existing power pole locations at property ends and verify that proposed sidewalk alignments maintain adequate clearance from pole structures, or document if poles must be relocated.

runComments.comment: Enlarged plan details must show existing power pole locations at property ends and document that proposed sidewalk alignments maintain adequate clearance from pole structures, or note if poles are to be relocated.

Plan view must clarify that new or modified sidewalks at each end of the property along right-of-way frontage are cleared of existing power poles, or if poles must be relocated to accommodate sidewalk.

comments.headline: Retaining wall clearances from overhead conductors
comments.summary: Section views for retaining walls must be provided with dimension annotations showing vertical and/or clearance spacing from outside conductor to wall face, demonstrating compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement where walls are near overhead electric lines.
comments.attn: Verify which retaining walls are located within potential clearance distance of OHE line at southern site boundary

details.text: Section views showing retaining wall elevations with dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall must be provided to demonstrate compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.

runComments.comment: Section views showing retaining wall elevations with dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall must be provided to demonstrate compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance requirement.
If retaining walls are located near overhead electric lines, provide section views with dimension annotations showing 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor to wall face.
Plan and section views must show dimensions from the outermost electric line to retaining wall faces, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained.

details.text: Section exhibits for retaining walls must show dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of each wall for clearance verification per UCM § 1.10.3.

runComments.comment: Section views for retaining walls near any overhead electric lines must include dimension annotations showing clearance from outside conductor to wall face.
Section exhibits must show dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of each retaining wall for clearance verification.

comments.headline: Vertical clearances and overhead conductor separation
comments.summary: Vertical clearance paths above transformer locations and horizontal clearances to overhead conductors are not documented. Cross-section drawings confirming adequate vertical clearance (7.5-foot minimum ground-to-sky) and radial separation from utility conductors (15-foot minimum from centerline) are not provided.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design must confirm presence/absence of adjacent overhead distribution lines and required separation distances.
comments.attn: Clarify whether any overhead distribution lines exist on adjacent properties or streets. If yes, obtain utility coordination documentation and cross-section drawings. Low confidence reflects limited information in current submission.

details.text: If overhead distribution lines exist on adjacent properties or streets, site plan does not document minimum 7.5-foot ground-to-sky vertical clearance extending above all transformer pads and proposed structures.

runComments.comment: If overhead distribution lines exist on adjacent properties or streets near transformer pad locations, provide site plan with dimensioned horizontal sky-to-ground clearances (minimum 7.5 feet) extending from ground to sky above all transformer pads and proposed structures.

details.text: If overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors exist on adjacent properties, dimensioned radii (minimum 15 feet from conductor centerline, not pole centerline) not shown for clearance from transformer pads and structures.

runComments.comment: If overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors are present on adjacent properties, provide site plan with dimensioned radii (minimum 15 feet measured from conductor centerline, not pole centerline) showing clearance from all transformer pad locations and proposed structures to overhead conductors.

details.text: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances from grade to overhead structures, roofs, overhangs, utility lines, and obstructions not provided. Site topography and clearances at transformer pad locations not verified.

runComments.comment: Cross-section drawings showing vertical clearances at transformer locations are not provided. If overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas exist above transformer access paths, submit cross-section drawings demonstrating adequate vertical clearance per UCM § 1.10.3 as required by Austin Energy Design.

Provide cross-section drawings at typical transformer pad locations showing vertical clearances from ground grade to any overhead structures, roofs, overhangs, utility lines, or other obstructions. Cross-sections should be at least at two locations representing the site's varied topography. Verify clearances meet UCM § 1.10.3 requirements.

details.text: If overhead distribution facilities exist on adjacent properties or streets, no confirmation provided that no buildings, parking garages, poles, signs, antennas, tanks, or other facilities are installed under or over overhead primary/neutral conductors.

runComments.comment: If overhead distribution facilities exist on adjacent properties or streets, confirm through site plan and utility notes that no customer buildings, parking garages, structures, poles, signs, antennas, tanks, or other facilities are installed under or over overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors.

comments.headline: Tree species compatibility and protective clearances
comments.summary: Proposed landscaping lacks utility-compatibility verification and proper clearance documentation. Tree species are not identified with ECM Appendix F utility-compatibility ratings, and root barrier specifications are not coordinated with transformer pad locations per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
comments.crossDep: Landscape architect must coordinate tree species and planting proximity with electrical utility clearance and root-barrier requirements.
comments.attn: Verify species names and utility-compatibility status from ECM Appendix F 'UC' column. Identify all trees within 10 lateral feet of pads or 15 lateral feet of overhead lines.

details.text: Tree species not identified with ECM Appendix F utility-compatibility ratings. All trees within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution must be 'UC' (Utility Compatible) species.

runComments.comment: Tree locations are shown on landscape plan but species are not identified with ECM Appendix F utility compatibility ratings. Submit tree species list with ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designations for all trees within 10 lateral feet of transformer pads or 15 lateral feet of overhead electric conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
Tree species and utility-compatibility status documented but spatial proximity of specific trees to transformer pads not correlated.

If non-compatible species are within these proximity ranges, relocation or removal must be shown.

details.text: Landscaping and shrub planting locations not correlated to transformer pad locations or access-door orientations. Minimum 10-foot clearance from access-door sides and 5-foot from non-access sides not dimensioned on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Landscaping is shown on site but clearance dimensions from plantings to transformer pads are not provided. Submit detailed planting plan with dimensions showing: (1) minimum 10 lateral feet clearance from shrubs/vegetation to transformer access door side, and (2) minimum 5 lateral feet clearance from other sides, per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
Shrub/vegetation planting locations not correlated to transformer pad locations or access door orientations.

Applicant must: (1) clearly identify access door orientation on each transformer pad on the electrical plan, (2) provide detailed landscape plan analysis showing minimum 10-foot clearance from transformer access door sides and minimum 5-foot clearance from non-access sides for all shrubs, groundcovers, and low-lying vegetation, with specific plant types and locations dimensioned.

details.text: Trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads not identified on landscape plan. Root barrier specifications (minimum 4-foot depth, installed 5 feet from equipment edge) not provided on landscape detail sheets.

runComments.comment: Trees within 20 lateral feet of transformers are not documented with root barrier details. Submit landscape detail sheets showing root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) for all trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
Root barrier requirements and details not shown; trees within 20-foot proximity of pads not identified.

Applicant must identify all trees on landscape plan (Sheet 31) that are located within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations (Sheet 21), and provide detailed root barrier specifications showing minimum 4-foot depth installed 5 feet from equipment edge. Include root barrier details on landscape detail sheet (Sheet 37) with cross-references to specific tree locations.

details.text: Underground electric equipment locations from the electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Clearance dimensions from proposed and retained trees to all underground equipment are not provided.
